body:
`$ --upload-log` sanitizes with its own `js/src/lib/log-sanitizer.js` and `rust/src/lib/log_sanitizer.rs`. Its false positives are in #249, and they are still present on main (0.39.1). We want one sanitizer for all our tools, link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer (link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer#42), used by gh-upload-log (https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-upload-log/issues/55) and hive-mind as well.

- Replace `js/src/lib/log-sanitizer.js` with link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer, or leave the masking to gh-upload-log once it does it. `rust/src/lib/log_sanitizer.rs` needs the same result: the library is JavaScript only, so the Rust build either calls its CLI or gh-upload-log, or link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer gets a Rust port.
- What start-command does well moves into that library first (link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer#42): masking values of secret-named environment variables, keeping non-UTF-8 bytes, 64 KB block streaming with continuation state, fail-closed private temporary file.
- Credentials only: account details in our logs are public and stay.
- The cases from #249 become regression tests.


The same move for the other two tools: link-foundation/gh-upload-log#55 and link-assistant/hive-mind#3740.
title: Use link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer for `$ --upload-log` instead of the own log-sanitizer
